scores.why: An agent-first companion for one condition: drug verdicts come from fixed data and the LLM only explains them, plus assistant intents, a watch heart monitor and a 13-language emergency card.
Concrete patient workflows: drug check by name, barcode (about 68k Polish packs bundled) or box photo, SOS countdown, doctor-visit brief; 74 real emulator screenshots.
About 38k ArkTS lines on the phone, 7k on the watch, 4k in edge functions; safety gate, response validator and offline fallback; nearly 600 tests; no committed secrets.
Intents, widgets, Live View, OCR, speech, Scan, NFC, user auth, push and a separate wearable app; phone and watch talk through the cloud rather than a native wearable channel.
The demo video is a rebuilt animation of the screens, not a recording of the running emulator.
Thorough README with exact versions, release with phone and watch packages, 389 small commits by 3 authors, detailed AI workflow docs.

projects.built_during_event: yes: 389 commits from 3 Oct 11:48 to 4 Oct 11:00 CEST
strengths: Widest native platform usage in the field
Safety design: deterministic verdicts, validator, offline fallback
592 automated tests plus a live LLM evaluation
Complete flows on phone and watch for a clear patient group
weaknesses: Demo video is an animation, not a recording
Heart rate, voice, NFC and push unverified on the emulator
Phone-watch link goes through the cloud
Very large scope makes depth hard to verify
red_flags: Mockup demo video despite the real-emulator requirement
Drug-risk data derived from a source with licence restrictions
projects.verdict: An exceptionally broad, polished, platform-heavy health companion, held back by a mockup demo video and features unverified on hardware.

scores.why: Offline mesh alerting is known (Briar, Bridgefy); signed authority alerts over NearLink plus an offline map of Kraków shelters is a fresh, platform-tied angle.
Real civil-protection need; the demo shows signing, two hops of relay and a forged copy rejected. Depends on official issuers and NearLink phones; relay only in the foreground.
Clean layers, canonical ECDSA verification, delivery queue with acknowledgements and retries, 177 host tests running the real sources, only 5 permissions, no secrets.
NearLink adapter, Crypto, Location, ArkData, Accessibility and a second OpenHarmony build; but the relay ran only over a laptop WebSocket hub, never NearLink hardware.
Narrated 2:58 video with a synchronized live recording of three emulators, speed-ups marked, and a 68-screen gallery.
Excellent README and team guide, checksummed releases, detailed AI workflow, explicit lists of what is real and what is simulated.

projects.built_during_event: yes: first commit 3 Oct 18:07 CEST (a 5.7k-line drop), 41 commits until 4 Oct 10:57
strengths: Rigorous signed-alert protocol against replay, expiry and tampering
Very honest about what is simulated
weaknesses: Small hand-written core compared with docs volume
Mostly one developer with heavy AI generation
red_flags: 5.7k-line first commit after about 7 hours hides early history
Demo mesh path is a laptop hub, not radio
projects.verdict: A carefully engineered, honest prototype whose key claim, phone-to-phone relay over NearLink, is unproven on devices.

calibration_note: Both well above a typical prototype and nearly tied: Celia leads on usefulness and platform breadth, SafeMesh on rigor and a real recorded demo.
